title: Girl, 9, says stepfather hits her with a belt (synthetic)
setting: Children's social worker Hannah Price visits Stacey Lambert and her daughter Millie (9) at 27 Orchard Way, Harbridge, after school reported Millie did not want to go home.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Hi, Stacey? I'm Hannah Price, the social worker from Harbridge children's services. We spoke this morning.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Come in. Millie's in the front room.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thanks. As I said on the phone, school contacted us because Millie told her teacher she didn't want to go home on Monday, and they asked us to check in.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: She's just been funny lately. It's the bedwetting, she's embarrassed.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. We'll talk about that. Um, first, what you and Millie tell me goes on our records, and I may need to share it with school, the GP or the police if I'm worried a child isn't safe. I'll always try to tell you if I'm doing that.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Is Craig in?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No, he's at work till six. He's on the bins.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Can I ask a bit about the family first? Who lives here?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Me, Millie, Craig, and our little one, Jayden, he's two. Craig's Millie's stepdad, we've been together four years.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And Millie's dad?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: He's in Scotland. She sees him summer holidays.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How are things with money and the house?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Alright. I do mornings at Greggs, Craig's full time. The landlord's slow fixing the damp in Millie's room though.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay, I can write to them about that. Stacey, would it be alright if I spoke to Millie on her own, in her room maybe? It's something we do with every child.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Yeah, fine. Millie, this is Hannah.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Hi Millie. Can I see your room? Your mum said you've got a hamster.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: She's called Biscuit. She's asleep.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: She's lovely. Millie, my job is to help make sure children are safe and happy. Is it okay if we have a chat?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You can say pass if you don't want to answer something. And if you tell me someone's hurting you, I can't keep that a secret, I'd have to tell people who can help. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: What do you like doing at school?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Art. And I'm in the netball team. Year Four.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Wow. And what's it like at home?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: It's okay. Jayden's annoying. He takes my pens.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Ha, little brothers. Your teacher said you didn't want to go home on Monday. Can you tell me about that?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Um. Because of the bed.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. What happens with the bed?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: When I wet the bed, Craig gets cross. He hits me with a belt.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you for telling me, Millie. Where does he hit you?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: On my legs. On the back of my legs.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: How many times has that happened?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Lots. Like every week. Every time I wet the bed.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: When was the last time?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Sunday. In the morning, before Mum got up.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Did it leave any marks?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Red lines. They went away.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Does anyone else at home hurt you?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: What about Mum, does Mum ever hit you?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: No. Mum never hits me. She gives me cuddles.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you. You've been really brave. None of this is your fault, not the bed, not anything.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Am I in trouble?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: No, you're not in trouble at all. I'm going to talk to your mum now, okay?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Stacey, Millie's told me that Craig hits her with a belt on her legs when she wets the bed, and that it happens about every week.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's not like that. It's just a smack. He gives her a smack with his belt now and again, on her legs, it's not hard.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Have you seen it happen?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Once or twice. He's from a strict family. I've told him to stop, but it's just a smack, it's not abuse.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I understand that's how it feels, but hitting a child with a belt isn't acceptable, and I have to act on it. I'm going to speak to my manager and the police today, that's called a strategy discussion.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Is he going to get arrested?

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I don't know yet. What I need today is for Millie to be safe tonight. Can Craig stay somewhere else?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: His brother's on Canal Street. He could go there.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Would you keep him away from the house until we've spoken again?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. I'll ring him now.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you. We might also ask a paediatrician to see Millie, I'll let you know.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: About the bedwetting, has she seen anyone?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. I thought she'd grow out of it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: The school nurse can refer her to the continence clinic, it's really common at her age. I'll ask them.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: That would help, the washing's endless.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: So, actions. I'll ring my manager and the police when I leave and call you by five today.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: You'll ring Craig now, and he'll stay at his brother's on Canal Street tonight.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll speak to Mrs Hollis at school tomorrow morning and ask the school nurse to refer Millie to the clinic.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll write to the landlord about the damp by Friday, and I'll visit again on Thursday the twenty-sixth.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay.

disclosures.what: Millie says her stepdad Craig hits her with a belt on the back of her legs when she wets the bed.
Millie says it happens every week, most recently on Sunday morning, and it left red lines.
Stacey says Craig gives Millie 'just a smack' with his belt on her legs and that she has seen it once or twice.
